transcript: Casey (vendor): Let me share my screen. This is the scheduling board; I will drag a shift to another day so you can see it update live. Sarah: We do not run our own servers. Casey: Good, because we do not offer a self-hosted edition. Sarah: The board looks good, but I cannot say whether it suits us until the supervisors have tried it. Can you give us a trial account? Casey: Yes, I will set one up by Thursday. transcript: Tom (seller): Thanks for making time. Carol (prospect): Our reps type every order in again by hand, which costs us about two days a month. My worry is that your tool needs a full data import before we see any benefit. Tom: Most customers import in one afternoon. Carol: Maybe, but I still expect IT to push back on yet another vendor login. We are also looking at Acme, which our parent company already uses. Tom: Could we start a pilot on the first of next month? Carol: I cannot agree to a start date before IT has seen your data-protection documents. Let us speak again next Wednesday. Tom: Wednesday works for me. Carol: If IT signs off and the pilot shows the time savings, we would buy twenty licences. I can approve up to 15000 euros on my own; anything above that goes to our finance director. Tom: I will send the data-protection documents today.
expectations: Two days a month lost to manual order entry; import-effort and IT-login objections kept even though Tom answered the first
Commitment is conditional: twenty licences only if IT signs off and the pilot shows the savings
Pilot start date proposed by Tom and not agreed; call next Wednesday proposed by Carol and accepted by Tom

transcript: Sam: Before we start, the onboarding guide for new hires is now published. Max: Nice work, the new hires already use it. One thing: your code reviews often arrive late in the day, which holds the others up. Sam: I see that differently. They arrive late because I am in customer calls every morning. Max: I still think reviews should come first. Sam: I disagree; the customer calls are what I was hired for. Max: Then let us try this: you block one hour after lunch for reviews for two weeks, and then we look at it again. Sam: Fine, two weeks. I would also like to attend the conference in May. Max: I cannot approve that myself. I will ask the budget owner this week, but I cannot promise anything. Sam: One more thing, your handover to me last quarter felt rushed. Max: Fair point, I will keep that in mind.
expectations: Onboarding guide published by Sam; feedback in both directions: Max on late reviews, Sam on a rushed handover
Disagreement kept with both positions attributed: Max wants reviews first, Sam prioritises morning customer calls

transcript: Sam: Vorweg, der Einarbeitungsleitfaden für neue Kolleginnen und Kollegen ist jetzt veröffentlicht. Max: Gute Arbeit, die Neuen nutzen ihn schon.
